1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bb5+ Nc6 4.O-O Bd7 5..strategy: Prepares a broad pawn centre while the bishop stays on b5. White follows a plain strategic plan and Black can develop without risk, since the exchange on c6 no longer doubles anything.

Backs up the bishop on b5 and the e-pawn and prepares an advance in the centre, but commits the queen early and leaves White with a less natural set-up than the plain developing moves. Black has time to complete a sound development.
Develops with tempo: the knight attacks the undefended e4, so White has to spend a move on it before the pawn centre can be built. Black keeps a solid, flexible position.

Prepares a fianchetto and a compact kingside, with the bishop on g7 to control the long diagonal. For the moment the move also loosens the diagonal towards h8, which is what White's central advance tries to use.
